title: Commented-Out Code (The Git-Ignored Remnant)
pattern: Valid syntactic expressions or blocks of code that have been commented out instead of being deleted.
why_bad: It creates fear among other maintainers, who assume the code is there for a critical reason and refuse to delete it. It clutters visual scanning and references defunct types or APIs.
detection: Block or line comments containing syntactically valid Rust expressions or declarations.
counterexample: Commented-out code blocks explicitly marked as examples in doc-tests or usage tutorials.
fix: Delete the commented-out code completely, relying on version control history to recover it if needed.
source: Robert C. Martin, *Clean Code* (2008), Chapter 4 ("Comments - Commented-Out Code"), pp. 68-69.
